title: PAIS Data Catalog
tagline: Papers, trials and disease burden for ME/CFS, long COVID and 120 other diseases.

sections.title: Research vs disease burden, 120 diseases
sections.finding: Papers and trials per year (2021–2025) set against global DALYs (GBD 2023) for 120 diseases. ME/CFS has 10.3× fewer papers (90% range 7.5–14.5) and 7.7× fewer trials (5.0–11.7) than the trend predicts for its burden. On papers, only neonatal encephalopathy falls further below. The trend is loose (R² 0.39 for papers, 0.38 for trials).

sections.title: Trials in all registries (WHO ICTRP)
sections.finding: ClinicalTrials.gov misses trials registered elsewhere. All registries hold 2.5× as many ME/CFS trials (1.8× without the two Chinese registries), against a median of 1.9× for 18 comparison diseases. Adjusted for this, the ME/CFS trial shortfall is about 6–8×. 29% of ME/CFS trials are not mainly in ME/CFS patients, between MS (17%) and RA (38%).

sections.title: Long COVID and ME/CFS trials
sections.finding: Long COVID trial starts peaked at 155 in 2023 and fell to 70 in 2025. ME/CFS stayed at 8–12 a year. Drug or biologic trials only: long COVID went from 47 in 2023 to 23 in 2025, and ME/CFS had 1–6 a year. In 2021–2025, 23% of long COVID drug trials had a commercial lead sponsor (32 of 141), and 8% of ME/CFS drug trials (1 of 13), against a median of 35% for 24 diseases with 10–30M DALYs.

sections.title: Research by which sex a disease mostly affects
sections.finding: After adjusting for burden, the share of patients who are women shows no detectable link with research volume across 120 diseases: 0.94× papers per +10 percentage points female (95% CI 0.79–1.11) and 0.99× trials (0.81–1.21). The female shares are hand-coded approximations.

sections.title: Public biomedical R&D funding and output, 2024
sections.finding: Government biomedical R&D budgets set against medical papers and citations, 19 countries. The US spends 32 bn PPS; China's budget is a guess (about 14 bn). Papers grow more slowly than budgets (log-log slope 0.76). Portugal publishes most per unit of budget, Japan and the US least. Seven budgets are estimates, so this is a rough signal, not an efficiency ranking.

data.about: One row per country or funder: 2024 budget (reported, estimated or guessed, with range and % of GDP), its split by funding type, medicine papers 1999–2024 and 2024 citations, and how each estimate was built. Compiled in a separate session; that code is not in the repo.

sections.title: Research vs disease burden, first 13 diseases
sections.finding: The first comparison used 13 well-funded chronic diseases. Against them ME/CFS had 20.3× fewer papers (90% range 12.5–30.6) and 13.4× fewer trials (8.9–18.8). These 13 sit above the broader trend, so they set a high bar. The 120-disease version gives about half these multiples.

sections.title: PAIS burden and ME
sections.finding: An illustrative model of post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) built on Dutch prevalence estimates. With the default assumptions, ME is about half of PAIS patients (1.5% of 3.1% of the population) but about 80% of the PAIS disease burden, because ME is much more disabling than most PAIS without ME. A second view sketches how Long COVID, ME, dysautonomia and MCAS may overlap. Every input can be changed on the topic page.
